author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Debugger Tutorial - PCSX2 | RetroAchievements (Reuploaded)
summary: CySlaytor documents a personal PCSX2 debugger workflow for finding stable pointers during RetroAchievements development, including a hexadecimal offset calculation while clearly separating the method from a universal step-by-step recipe.

blocks.text: This reuploaded tutorial is useful because it frames pointer hunting as an investigative practice rather than a magic address list. The creator shows the approach that works in their own achievement-authoring sessions and adds a concrete calculation: subtract a candidate pointer value from the target address in Windows Calculator’s programmer mode to derive a larger hexadecimal offset. Within RetroAchievements work, that relation can help an author move from a volatile runtime location toward memory logic that survives a restart or a different gameplay state.

The author explicitly says the approach is not one-size-fits-all. Pointer-chain depth, game revision, allocator behavior and validation across resets remain outside the published example. A numerical offset can be internally consistent yet still point to unrelated memory after a level transition. Use the debugger on legally obtained software, document the supported hash, retest from cold boot and seek peer review under current RetroAchievements authoring rules. The example teaches a reasoning tool; it does not certify an achievement condition by itself.
